tags.name: Tags
tags.description: A tag allows to categorize a counting site. It help to get quickly traffic data for specific categories.

tags.name: Sites
tags.description: A counting site represents a location equipped with one or many traffic counting systems.

parameters.description:
Request additional information in response by using `include` request parameter.

<u>Historical weather data (forecast)</u>

**Our historical weather data is forecast data and not actuals.**
Adding weather in the include parameter, you can access historical weather data associated to your traffic.

<u>Data status</u>

Adding status in the include parameter, you can get the data status indicator : raw, modified, validated, etc.

| Possible values      | Description                |
|----------------------|----------------------------|
| status               | Returns the data status.   |
| weather              | Returns the weather data.  |

post.summary: Validate the data of the given sites on a period
post.description:
Validate the data of the given sites from their ids on a period. The process is asynchronous.
Restrictions:
- Only one job can be in progress per API key
- The validation period cannot exceed 1 year
- Maximum 10 sites can be validated at once

siteIds.description:
The array of Eco-Visio identifiers of the sites.
Maximum 10 sites can be validated at once.

startDate.description:
The start date of the period to validate. startDate is inclusive. Full-date notation defined by RFC 3339 ; example : 2023-09-20
The validation period cannot exceed 1 year from startDate to endDate.

endDate.description:
The end date of the period to validate. endDate is exclusive. Full-date notation defined by RFC 3339 ; example : 2023-09-20
The validation period cannot exceed 1 year from startDate to endDate.

Position.description:
GeoJson fundamental geometry construct.
A position is an array of numbers. There MUST be two or more elements. The first two elements are longitude and latitude, or easting and northing, precisely in that order and using decimal numbers. Altitude or elevation MAY be included as an optional third element.
Implementations SHOULD NOT extend positions beyond three elements because the semantics of extra elements are unspecified and ambiguous. Historically, some implementations have used a fourth element to carry a linear referencing measure (sometimes denoted as "M") or a numerical timestamp, but in most situations a parser will not be able to properly interpret these values. The interpretation and meaning of additional elements is beyond the scope of this specification, and additional elements MAY be ignored by parsers.

LineStringCoordinates.description: GeoJSon fundamental geometry construct, array of two or more positions.

LineString.description: GeoJson geometry object, array of two or more positions that share a relationship.

schema.description:
Export schema format for structuring mobility data:
  - **mobility_counting_schema** : comprehensive mobility counting format designed for interoperability and standardization. 
    The format uses CSV files organized in a logical hierarchy, making it easy to process with standard data tools while maintaining data integrity and completeness.

    📋 [Complete schema documentation](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1u2S_TVG2tT2BorHWI2syjrisXH49SH4m-PFKE3Mj840/edit#heading=h.gsqclrqliggp)

  |----------------------|----------------------|
  | PT15M                | 15 minutes           |
  | PT1H                 | 1 hour               |
  | P1D                  | 1 day                |
  | P1M                  | 1 month              |
  | P1Y                  | 1 year               |

validatedDataOnly.description: Filter the results to include only validated data. If set to true, only data that has been validated will be returned. If set to false or not specified, all data will be returned.

gapFilling.description: Fill gaps with null values to ensure contiguous series. If set to true, gaps will be filled with "null". If set to false or not specified, gaps will remain unfilled.

validateSchema.description:
Enable strict schema validation to ensure data compliance and completeness.

When enabled (`true`), the export process will:
* Verify all required fields are present and properly formatted
* Validate data types and value constraints
* Fail the export if any validation errors are found

When disabled (`false`, default), missing optional fields will be handled gracefully, and the export will proceed with available data.

**Note**: Enable validation when preparing data for import to ensure full compliance with national data portal requirements.
